data.title: Journey Through the Solar System
data.description: Explore the unique characteristics, atmospheres, and sizes of our solar system's most fascinating planets.
data.introduction: Welcome, space explorers! Today we will travel across the solar system to discover what makes different worlds unique.
data.celebration: Fantastic job, cadet! You have successfully completed your mission across our solar system.

planets.description: Earth is our home and the only known world with liquid water on its surface. It has a protective atmosphere that allows life to thrive.
planets.funFact: Earth is the only planet not named after a Greek or Roman god or goddess.
planets.transition: Now, let us journey to our scorching neighbor closer to the Sun.

questions.question: Which of these is a unique feature of Earth compared to many other inner planets?
questions.explanation: Earth is the only known planet with abundant liquid water on its surface.

questions.question: What is the length of a day on Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth rotates on its axis once every 24 hours.

planets.description: Venus is covered in thick clouds of sulfuric acid and has a runaway greenhouse effect. This traps heat and makes it the hottest planet.
planets.funFact: Venus spins in the opposite direction of most other planets in the solar system.
planets.transition: Next, let us travel outward to the famous red world.

questions.question: Which planet has a higher surface temperature, Earth or Venus?
questions.explanation: Venus has a thick atmosphere of carbon dioxide that traps heat, making it much hotter than Earth.

questions.question: How does the number of moons on Venus compare to Earth?
options: Venus has more moons than Earth
Both have the same number of moons
Venus has fewer moons than Earth
questions.explanation: Venus has zero moons, while Earth has one moon.

planets.description: Mars is a cold, rocky desert with a very thin atmosphere. Iron oxide on its surface gives it a distinct rusty red color.
planets.funFact: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, the largest volcano in the solar system.
planets.transition: Let us journey further out to the giant of the solar system.

questions.question: Which planet has a longer day, Earth or Mars?
options: Both have the exact same day length
questions.explanation: Mars takes about 24.6 hours to complete one rotation, which is slightly longer than Earth's 24-hour day.

questions.question: Comparing Mars and Venus, which planet has more moons?
options: Both have the same number of moons
questions.explanation: Mars has 2 moons (Phobos and Deimos), while Venus has 0 moons.

planets.description: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, made mostly of swirling gases and liquids. It features the famous Great Red Spot, a giant storm.
planets.funFact: Jupiter has dozens of moons, including Ganymede, which is bigger than the planet Mercury.

questions.question: Which planet is much larger in diameter, Earth or Jupiter?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system and is more than 11 times wider than Earth.

questions.question: Comparing Jupiter and Mars, which planet has a shorter day length?
options: Both have the same day length
questions.explanation: Jupiter rotates extremely fast, completing a full day in only 9.9 hours compared to Mars' 24.6 hours.
